_README: Eval suite for the ITL corpus. Schema per case: q (the question); outcome: answered | clarify | rejected; keywords_all (case-insensitive substrings that MUST appear); keywords_absent (substrings that must NOT appear); reference (ground truth for the LLM grader); grade: true enables LLM grading; new_session: true starts a fresh conversation (omit to test a follow-up against the previous case); product scopes retrieval; requires_deepseek: true skips the case when no key is configured. Every fact below is copied from a REVIEWED FAQ answer in faq_store.json, so the ground truth is human-approved rather than invented. Workflow: python eval.py --update-baseline to lock, then python eval.py after every change. The previous contents of this file were the unedited template placeholders ('<YOUR PRODUCT>'), which is why eval_baseline.json was meaningless and those literal strings appear as real queries in logs.jsonl.

cases.q: What is MyCheckr?
cases.reference: MyCheckr is an all-in-one device solution that performs anonymous age estimation, to assist with the sale of age-restricted goods.

cases.q: Does MyCheckr need an internet connection?
cases.reference: No. MyCheckr provides instant results with no requirement for internet, and features local processing requiring no cloud base access.

cases.q: Does MyCheckr store personal data?
cases.reference: No data is stored. MyCheckr is GDPR certified by the Age Check Certification Scheme (ACCS).

cases.q: Who certified MyCheckr for GDPR?
cases.reference: MyCheckr is GDPR certified by the Age Check Certification Scheme (ACCS).

cases.q: Are there recurring fees for MyCheckr?
cases.reference: No. It is a one-off payment for the device with no recurring fees.

cases.q: Which retailing strategy does MyCheckr automate?
cases.reference: The checking process automates the Challenge 25 retailing strategy, to restrict illegal sales of age-restricted items to underage customers.

cases.q: How can MyCheckr be mounted?
cases.reference: MyCheckr can be mounted using a VESA Mount and 1/4 inch screws, on a pole or a wall.

cases.q: Does MyCheckr require integration with other systems?
cases.reference: No. It is an all-in-one device; integration is optional but not required. It is however compatible with host machines for integration via API.

cases.q: What hardware does MyCheckr include?
cases.reference: It comes equipped with an inbuilt camera and a display screen.

cases.q: What voltage is supported on the NV9ST?
cases.reference: The NV9ST supports 12VDC.

cases.q: How does the NV9USB+ communicate with a host?
cases.reference: Host communication is via USB or TTL.

cases.q: Can the NV9 USB+ be mounted vertically?
cases.reference: The NV9 USB+ can be mounted horizontally or vertically.

cases.q: What is the note capacity of the NV11+ Note Float recycler?
cases.reference: The add-on Note Float recycler for the NV11+ has a capacity of 30 notes.

cases.q: Can national currency differences affect cashbox capacity on the NV9USB+?
cases.reference: Some national currencies differ in thickness and circulation practices; depending on usage this can impact cashbox capacities by 10-15%. Consult an ITL representative for details.

cases.q: What are typical applications for the NV9USB+ range?
cases.reference: Typical applications include amusement, vending, gaming, and low-volume retail.

cases.q: Can the NV9USB+ recycle notes?
cases.reference: A Note Float module can be added to provide note recycling capability. The add-on recycler for the NV11+ holds 30 notes.

cases.q: What is the SMART Coin System?
cases.reference: The SMART Coin System is a bulk coin validator, mixed coin hopper and recycler in one. It validates, discriminates and stores mixed coins, eliminating coin starvation and the need for multiple hoppers.

cases.q: How many coins per second does the SMART Coin System handle?
cases.reference: The SMART Coin System operates at a market leading 12 coins per second.

cases.q: What problem does the SMART Coin System eliminate?
cases.reference: It eliminates coin starvation and the need for multiple hoppers.

cases.q: What is the standard lid assembly for the SMART Hopper?
cases.reference: The standard lid assembly for the SMART Hopper is PA02051 - Lid Assembly. PA02698 is a DIFFERENT part: the Twin SMART Coin System Secondary Hopper Lid Assembly. The two must not be confused.

cases.q: What is the standard lid assembly for the Twin SMART Coin System?
cases.reference: The standard lid assembly for the Twin SMART Coin System is PA02698 - Twin SMART Coin System Secondary Hopper Lid Assembly. PA02051 is the plain SMART Hopper lid and is a different part.

cases.q: What is the standard nozzle option for the SMART Hopper?
cases.reference: The standard nozzle option for the SMART Hopper is PM00488 - Top Pay Nozzle. PM01106 is the pay-in chute Funnel, a different part.

cases.q: What is the standard pay in chute option for the SMART Coin System Range?
cases.reference: The standard pay in chute option is PM01106 - Funnel. PM00488 is the Top Pay Nozzle, a different part.

cases.q: Which chute option collects debris?
cases.reference: The chute option for debris collection is PA04138 - Chute with Debris Collection.

cases.q: What are the three key components of the MyConnect Environment?
cases.reference: The three key components are the MyConnect Hub, the MyConnect App (Android), and MyCheckr Devices.

cases.q: How does the MyConnect App talk to the MyConnect Hub?
cases.reference: The MyConnect App communicates with the MyConnect Hub using REST API and multicast discovery.

cases.q: how fast is it?
cases.reference: Follow-up test, no new_session: 'it' must resolve to the SMART Coin System from the previous case, giving 12 coins per second.

cases.q: what voltage does it need
cases.reference: Underspecified and unscoped: voltage is documented for several different products, so the correct behaviour is to ask which one rather than to pick one.

cases.q: how do I mount it
cases.reference: Unscoped: MyCheckr mounts via VESA, the NV9 USB+ mounts horizontally or vertically. Two different answers, so ask which product.

cases.q: what is the capital of france
cases.reference: Plainly off-domain. Must refuse rather than answer from general knowledge.

cases.q: how do I reset the password on my Cisco router
cases.reference: Adversarial guard: shares vocabulary with the corpus (reset, password, network) but is about unrelated hardware. Domain-adjacent wording must not produce a confident answer from unrelated chunks. This is the exact shape that once retrieved a stray password-policy chunk and generated a confident walkthrough at 0.055 grounding.

cases.q: what is the bitcoin price today
cases.reference: Off-domain and time-sensitive. Nothing in the corpus supports it.

cases.q: does the SMART Coin System support facial recognition
cases.reference: Adversarial cross-product guard: facial/age estimation belongs to MyCheckr, not the coin validator. Must not borrow MyCheckr's capabilities to answer about the SMART Coin System.

cases.q: what is the maximum coin capacity in litres of the SMART Coin System
cases.reference: The reviewed answers claim 'market leading coin capacity' without stating a figure. Inventing a number is the failure being guarded against; refusing is correct unless the manual states it.
